help.auditRetentionDays: How many days audit events are kept before the worker deletes them.
help.expiredSessionRetentionDays: How many days an ended session is kept, counted from the expiry of its token family, before the worker deletes it.
help.exportRetentionDays: How many days a GDPR data export stays downloadable before it is deleted.
help.objectPurgeDelayDays: How many days a deleted file is kept in storage before it is purged for good. Must exceed the number of daily backup snapshots, so every backup can still restore its files.
help.refreshGraceSeconds: For how many seconds an already used refresh token is still accepted, so two tabs refreshing at the same moment are not mistaken for a stolen token.
help.sessionIdleSeconds: After how many seconds without activity a session ends. Must not exceed the absolute session lifetime.
help.sessionAbsoluteSeconds: After how many seconds a session ends however active it is; then the person logs in again.
help.maxUploadBytes: The largest file one upload may have, in bytes. Must stay below the Nginx body size ceiling.
help.userQuotaBytes: How many bytes of files one person may store in total.
help.totalQuotaBytes: How many bytes of files the whole application may store.
help.backupSchedule: When the backup runs, as a five-field cron expression in Europe/Berlin time. The backup alert expects one run a day, so change it together with the alert.
help.backupRetentionDailySnapshots: How many daily backup snapshots are kept.
help.rateLimitSamlLoginPerMinute: How many TU-ID logins one client IP may start per minute. Generous, because a university network puts many people behind few addresses.
help.rateLimitSamlAcsPerMinute: How many answers from the identity provider one client IP may return per minute.
help.rateLimitRefreshPerMinute: How many session refreshes one client IP may make per minute.
help.rateLimitPasswordLoginPerMinute: How many break-glass password attempts one account may make per client IP and minute.
help.rateLimitUploadsPerMinute: How many files one person may upload per minute. An API token counts as its owner.
help.rateLimitDataExportsPerMinute: How many GDPR data exports one person may start per minute.
help.rateLimitMailCampaignsPerMinute: How many mail campaigns one person may send per minute.
help.rateLimitUpdateChecksPerMinute: How many times per minute one person may ask for the update check now.
help.rateLimitDirectorySearchPerMinute: How many directory searches one person may make per minute. Each is an LDAP query.
help.rateLimitSiteLookupPerMinute: How many location lookups one person may make per minute. Each is a request to NetBox.
help.mailSendLimitCount: How many mails may be sent per window, across all worker processes.
help.mailSendLimitWindowSeconds: The length of the mail sending window, in seconds.
help.mailDeliveryRetentionDays: How many days the delivery log keeps who got which mail, in which wording.
help.featureFlags: Named switches for features, as an object of name to true or false. Empty unless a product defines some.
help.maintenanceMode: While on, only those who may manage settings use the application; everyone else's sessions end and the worker pauses. Switched with the button above.
help.viewAsMinutes: How many minutes a read-only view as another person lasts. It is never extended.

exports.title: My data
exports.explainOwn: Download everything this system holds about you, as a ZIP file with a JSON document and your files. It is prepared in the background and kept for a few days.
exports.failedHint: This export could not be prepared. Please request a new one.

gdpr.explain: Requests of data subjects: find the person by TU-ID, export their data to hand it over, or erase them.
gdpr.exportExplain: The export is available to you only. Hand it over to the person yourself.
gdpr.eraseExplain: Removes TU-ID, name, email and picture, deletes the person's documents and files and logs them out everywhere. The account remains only as an anonymous number in the activity log. This cannot be undone.
gdpr.notSelf: You cannot erase your own account.
gdpr.notBreakGlass: The break-glass account holds no personal data and cannot be erased.

apiTokens.intro: An API token lets a script call the API over REST with the permissions chosen for it, never more than its owner holds at the time of the call. Send it in the Authorization header:
apiTokens.name: Name
apiTokens.permissionsHint: Only permissions you hold yourself, and none that need a person in the browser
apiTokens.nothingGrantable: You hold no permission a token may carry.
apiTokens.expiresHint: Leave empty for a token that lasts until it is revoked
apiTokens.createdText: Copy it now: it is not stored and will not be shown again. Anyone who has it can act with its permissions.
apiTokens.revokeConfirm: Revoke the token “{name}”? Scripts using it stop working at once.

permissions.title: Roles & permissions
permissions.intro: A role is a set of permissions; a person has all permissions of all their roles and of “Everyone signed in”. Their own user record, their data export and ending a view-as no role can take from anybody. Administration always has every permission and alone manages roles. Who may add or change something may also read it, and who may delete it may also change it, as far as the permission reaches.
permissions.keyHint: Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens; fixed once created
permissions.name: Name ({locale})
permissions.assigned: The role is still assigned. Remove it from everybody who holds it first.
permissions.previewing: Preview as “{name}”: menus and actions as this role shows them. Data is still read with your own rights.

permissions.everyone: Everyone signed in holds it without an assignment; editable, not deletable

viewAs.banner: You see the application as {who}, read-only, until {until}. What you may not see yourself stays hidden.

maintenance.title: Maintenance
maintenance.body: The application is being maintained and is not available right now. This page checks every 30 seconds and takes you to the login as soon as it is back.
maintenance.banner: Maintenance mode is on: only administrators can use the application.
maintenance.isOn: On: only people who may change settings can log in; everyone else sees the maintenance page, API tokens are refused and the worker takes no jobs.
maintenance.confirmEnable: Everyone who may not change settings is logged out at once and sent to the maintenance page, cannot log in until it is over, and API tokens are refused. The worker stops taking jobs.
maintenance.confirmDisable: Everyone can log in again, API tokens work again and the worker resumes its jobs.
maintenance.loginHint: Maintenance mode is on: only administrators can log in.

systemInfo.eolSoon: No end of life soon | One release line ends within 90 days | {n} release lines end within 90 days
systemInfo.driftHint: The running version is not the pinned one: an image rebuilt but not restarted, or overridden in production.
